name: Titanium Dioxide (TiO2) Pigment: Domestic Producers Behind a Re-imposed Anti-Dumping Duty
scope: India imports ~75-79% of its TiO2 pigment (paints 60%, plastics 25%; ~62% from China) and the Finance Ministry re-imposed a 5-year anti-dumping duty of USD 460-681/t on Chinese TiO2 on 24 Oct 2026 (Notification 26/2026-Customs (ADD)) after a ~13-month gap; listed exposure is narrow: Meghmani Organics via Kilburn Chemicals (~18% of capacity, plant had been shut on the duty lapse, stock down ~30% YoY) is the only operating listed producer, while Adani Enterprises is an upstream option leg (subsidiary Alluvial Heavy Minerals holds ~991 ha of APMDC ilmenite leases; the group's ~Rs 16,000 cr TiO2/slag/sponge plan is only a state-briefed proposal). Early, thinly covered and not re-rated, but effectively a single-producer turnaround.
questions: What is TiO2 pigment (sulphate vs chloride process, anatase vs rutile grades), what end markets drive demand (paints/coatings ~60%, plastics ~25%) and what is the growth outlook for India and globally?

What exactly did the 24 Oct 2026 anti-dumping notification (26/2026-Customs (ADD)) impose: rates by producer, exemptions (food, pharma, nano grades), duration, and why was the earlier May 2025 duty quashed by the Calcutta High Court and how durable is the new one against further legal challenge?

How large is India's TiO2 import dependence and who are the domestic producers (Kerala Minerals & Metals, Travancore Titanium Products, V.V. Titanium, Kilburn/Meghmani) and which of them are actually listed on NSE/BSE?

What is Meghmani Organics' TiO2 position through Kilburn Chemicals at Dahej (capacity, process, grade, utilisation), what did management say about the plant shutdown during the duty lapse, and what restart/utilisation and phase-2 expansion plans has it stated since the duty returned?

Has Adani Enterprises, Adani Ports or any other listed company itself announced (board approval, exchange filing, investor presentation) a TiO2 or ilmenite-to-pigment project, versus the Andhra Pradesh government disclosure of an Adani Group Srikakulam proposal (200,000 tpa TiO2, ~Rs 16,000 cr, Oct 2026)? What is its real status?

Is there any other listed Indian company already making, qualifying or planning TiO2, titanium slag or rutile feedstock (e.g. mineral sands, chemical or paint-group backward integration)? Check small, mid and large caps explicitly.

How much pricing power does the duty give domestic producers: landed cost of Chinese TiO2 before/after duty, Chinese price cycle and channel inventory, and the earnings sensitivity of Meghmani to TiO2 utilisation and realisations?
Has the market priced this in? Stock performance of Meghmani over 1/3/6/12 months, and broker, media or thematic coverage of TiO2 stocks to date.

What are the risks: re-litigation of the duty, Chinese price cuts and third-country re-routing, cost inflation in sulphuric acid and ilmenite, higher input costs for paint makers (Asian Paints, Berger, Kansai Nerolac) and any pass-through or margin squeeze?
What are the near-term catalysts (Q3 FY27 results and plant restart commentary, customs enforcement and any court challenge, Adani project approvals and mining leases, Chinese export price moves)?

domestic_tio2_producers: Listed companies with an operating TiO2 pigment plant in India that benefit directly from the import-duty reset
planned_integrated_capacity: Listed companies with company-disclosed ilmenite/beach-sand mining aimed at TiO2 value-addition; the TiO2 plant itself is a group proposal briefed to the state, not yet a company filing (inference, not confirmed intent)
